title: Galaxy Phones Receiving One UI 9: Full List, Release Dates & Update Schedule Revealed
body:
Samsung has begun the phased rollout of One UI 9, its latest Android 17‑based skin, bringing a suite of visual refinements, performance tweaks and new features to a select group of Galaxy devices. While flagship models such as the Galaxy S24 series receive the update this week, many mid‑range and older flagships will have to wait weeks or months before the upgrade lands on their screens. The rollout marks Samsung’s most ambitious software push in recent years, underscoring its strategy to keep the Android ecosystem vibrant across a wide hardware spectrum.

The first wave of the update targets the newest generation of Samsung’s premium lineup. The Galaxy S24, S24+, and S24 Ultra are already receiving the One UI 9 build, which introduces a refreshed notification shade, revamped quick settings, and a more cohesive dark‑mode experience. Alongside aesthetic changes, Samsung has integrated deeper AI‑driven assistance, including contextual suggestions in the camera app and smarter battery management that learns usage patterns to extend endurance. Early user reports suggest the upgrade runs smoothly, with most devices completing the installation within 30 minutes and showing modest improvements in app launch times.

Following the flagship rollout, Samsung is extending One UI 9 to its high‑end mid‑range offerings. The Galaxy A54, A74 and the recently launched Galaxy Z Fold 5 and Z Flip 5 are slated to receive the update over the next two weeks. These devices will benefit from the same core UI overhaul while retaining hardware‑specific optimizations, such as the Fold series’ multitasking enhancements and the A‑series’ camera‑centric features. Samsung’s decision to prioritize these models reflects a broader industry trend: manufacturers are increasingly using software as a differentiator, especially for devices that sit between premium flagships and budget phones.

Older flagships, including the Galaxy S23 series and the Note 20 Ultra, are also on the upgrade list but will see the update later in the month. Samsung has indicated that devices launched before 2022 may experience a delayed rollout due to the need for additional testing and driver updates. Meanwhile, legacy models such as the Galaxy S22, S21 and older Note devices will not receive One UI 9 at all, as Samsung shifts its support window toward newer hardware. Users of these phones will continue to receive security patches but will miss out on the full suite of new features, a move that may accelerate upgrade cycles among long‑time Samsung enthusiasts.

Industry analysts view the rollout as a strategic maneuver to maintain Samsung’s dominance in the Android market. By delivering a consistent, feature‑rich experience across a broad portfolio, Samsung aims to lock users into its ecosystem, reducing the appeal of competing manufacturers that often lag in software updates. The inclusion of Android 17, with its emphasis on privacy controls, on‑device AI, and enhanced multitasking, aligns Samsung’s roadmap with Google’s vision while allowing the company to layer its own innovations on top. This balance of collaboration and differentiation could set a new benchmark for how OEMs handle major OS upgrades.

Looking ahead, Samsung’s roadmap suggests that One UI 9 will serve as the foundation for future enhancements, including deeper integration with the company’s wearable and smart‑home products. The company has hinted at upcoming features such as cross‑device continuity, expanded support for Samsung DeX, and richer customization options for the new Material‑You‑inspired design language. As the rollout progresses, users will be watching closely for any stability issues, but early feedback points to a polished experience that could reinforce Samsung’s reputation for delivering timely, high‑quality software updates.
